facts.raw_span: a 10-day history of a pruritic eruption
denied contact allergens, fever, or hyperhidrosis
no prior history of atopic dermatitis, dermatophytosis, or hand eczema
scleral icterus
multiple dusky, thin plaques with a central collarette of scale on the face, neck, axillae, trunk, and extremities
hyperkeratotic plaques and deeply seated vesicles with a greenish-black hue, especially accentuated along the dermatoglyphic ridges
total bilirubin 28.9 mg/dL
direct bilirubin 17.7 mg/dL
AST 78 IU/L
psoriasiform epidermal acanthosis, intraepidermal spongiosis, hyperkeratosis with sparse perivascular lymphocytic inflammation, and a dilated eccrine duct containing amorphous pink material
Gram, periodic acid–Schiff, and iron stains were negative
punch biopsies of the chest and thigh were consistent with pityriasis rosea

concepts.why: The patient has scleral icterus and elevated bilirubin levels, which are consistent with a diagnosis of primary biliary cholangitis.
The patient has a pruritic eruption with multiple dusky, thin plaques, and punch biopsies of the chest and thigh are consistent with pityriasis rosea.
The patient has hyperkeratotic plaques and deeply seated vesicles, and a punch biopsy of the right palm reveals psoriasiform epidermal acanthosis and intraepidermal spongiosis.
The patient has elevated bilirubin levels and scleral icterus, which are consistent with a diagnosis of cholestasis.
The patient has a pruritic eruption with multiple dusky, thin plaques, which is consistent with a viral exanthem.
The patient has hyperkeratotic plaques and deeply seated vesicles, which are consistent with a diagnosis of lichen planus.
The patient has elevated liver enzymes and bilirubin levels, which are consistent with a diagnosis of autoimmune hepatitis.
The patient has elevated liver enzymes and bilirubin levels, which are consistent with a diagnosis of drug-induced liver injury.

rationales.F01: Pruritic eruption is a common symptom of various skin conditions, but the presence of a pruritic eruption does not strongly rule in or out any of the listed concepts.
rationales.F04: Scleral icterus is a sign of liver disease, which is consistent with Primary Biliary Cholangitis, Cholestasis, and Autoimmune Hepatitis.
rationales.F07: Elevated total bilirubin is a sign of liver disease, which is consistent with Primary Biliary Cholangitis, Cholestasis, and Autoimmune Hepatitis.
rationales.F08: Elevated direct bilirubin is a sign of liver disease, which is consistent with Primary Biliary Cholangitis, Cholestasis, and Autoimmune Hepatitis.
rationales.F09: Elevated AST is a sign of liver disease, which is consistent with Primary Biliary Cholangitis, Cholestasis, Autoimmune Hepatitis, and Drug-Induced Liver Injury.
rationales.F12: Punch biopsies of the chest and thigh were consistent with Pityriasis Rosea, which strongly rules in this concept.

frontier_selector.rationale: The patient's presentation of scleral icterus, elevated total and direct bilirubin levels, and lack of contradictions support cholestasis as the most likely diagnosis.
